claims.text: Controlled post-deposition rapid thermal annealing can refine an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating to a nanocrystalline grain size of approximately 10–40 nm.
A nanocrystalline FeNiCrCoCu coating will have better high-temperature wear resistance than a coarser-grained as-deposited coating.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating on steel has a coarse, heterogeneous grain structure.
Rapid thermal annealing can produce the target nanocrystalline structure without unwanted grain growth or over-oxidation.
High grain-boundary density provides nucleation sites for a uniform, continuous protective oxide layer.
At high temperature, oxide coverage and oxide-layer stability increase and can protect the underlying metallic material during sliding.
The protective tribofilm on FeNiCrCoCu is likely enriched in oxidized Cr and/or Cu species.
The nanocrystalline structure causes the protective oxide to form more rapidly and persist during wear.
A continuous oxide tribofilm reduces localized stress and accommodates strain.
The oxide tribofilm delays microcrack initiation and crack propagation.
Formation of a protective oxide layer improves wear resistance.
The annealed nanocrystalline coating will exhibit a lower wear rate than the coarse-grained baseline.
The annealed nanocrystalline coating will exhibit smoother and more uniform wear tracks.
A more continuous protective oxide layer will improve frictional stability.
The proposed mechanism applies around 600 °C in ambient air under representative high-temperature sliding loads and speeds.
Behavior outside the specified temperature and loading range is uncertain.
Unintended grain growth or over-oxidation may offset the benefits of annealing outside the controlled regime.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant wear-rate reduction, smoother tracks, or a continuous oxide layer relative to the as-deposited control would falsify the proposed nanocrystallinity-mediated mechanism.
